How many coefficients does an image need before it looks like itself? Choose a
basis, then move the **keep** slider below the images. Start at 5% and compare
Fourier, the DCT (discrete cosine transform), and the wavelets on the same
photograph. For the reasoning behind
the experiment, read [Compression via Sparsity](compression-via-sparsity.qmd).

The experiment keeps the largest coefficients **in absolute value**, across
all three RGB channels together. It measures reconstruction error, not encoded
file size. The transforms run locally in your browser and require WebGPU.

```{ojs}
  const random = Inputs.button("Random photo", { label: "or" })
  // The label is only a visual "or"; without this it would be the button's name.

  const set = (value) => {
    form.value = value
    form.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }))
  }
  url.addEventListener("input", (e) => { e.stopPropagation(); set(url.value) })
  random.addEventListener("input", (e) => {

  })
  file.addEventListener("input", (e) => { e.stopPropagation(); if (file.value) set(file.value) })
  form.value = url.value
```

```{ojs}
// The slider runs on a log scale from one coefficient to all of them, which is
// the plot's rank axis shifted by a constant, so the thumb stays over the
// plot's dashed line. It is rebuilt for each image size but keeps its value.
keepInput = {
  const n = 3 * image.h * image.w
  const lo = Math.log10(100 / n)
  const keep = Math.min(100, Math.max(100 / n, this?.value ?? 5))
  const range = html`<input type="range" aria-label="coefficients kept, log scale" min=${lo} max="2" step="any" value=${Math.log10(keep)}>`
  const at = (d) => `calc(${(100 * (d - lo)) / (2 - lo)}%)`
  const form = html`<div class="keep-slider playground-wide">
    <div class="label">keep<br>(log)</div>
    ${range}
    <div class="ticks">${d3.range(Math.ceil(lo), 3).map((d) =>
      html`<span style="left: ${at(d)}">${+(10 ** d).toPrecision(1)}%</span>`)}</div>
  </div>`
  form.value = keep
  range.addEventListener("input", () => { form.value = 10 ** range.valueAsNumber })
  return form
}
```

```{ojs}
// The decay curve and, on its own axis, the share of the energy kept by
// stopping at each rank: it climbs as coefficients are added, steeply at first
// because most of the energy is in the largest few. The dashed line is the
// slider's cut.
{
  const { curve, n } = analysis
  // The energy is plotted by its nines, -log10(1 - energy), so 90%, 99% and
  // 99.9% are evenly spaced, and that range is mapped onto the magnitude's log
  // range so the two curves share the plot's height. The last coefficients
  // push the count towards infinity and into float rounding, so the axis
  // stops at five nines, 99.999%, and the curve is clipped there.
  const nines = (e) => -Math.log10(1 - e)
  const top = 5
  const extent = d3.extent(curve, (d) => Math.log10(d.magnitude))
  const m0 = extent[0], m1 = Math.max(extent[1], m0 + 1)
  const y = (k) => 10 ** (m0 + (Math.min(k, top) / top) * (m1 - m0))
  const ninesLabel = (k) => k === 0 ? "0%" : k === 1 ? "90%" : `99${k > 2 ? "." + "9".repeat(k - 2) : ""}%`
  return html`<div class="playground-wide">${Plot.plot({
    ...plotBase,
    width: wideWidth,
    height: 340,
    marginLeft: 60,
    marginRight: 60,
    marginBottom: 52,
    x: { type: "log", domain: [1, n], label: "rank (coefficients, largest first)", labelAnchor: "center", labelOffset: 42, grid: true },
    y: { type: "log", domain: [10 ** m0, 10 ** m1], axis: null },
    marks: [
      Plot.gridY({ strokeOpacity: 0.07 }),
      Plot.axisY({ anchor: "left", label: "↑ magnitude", color: col.series[0] }),
      Plot.axisY(d3.range(0, top + 1), {
        anchor: "right", y, tickFormat: ninesLabel, label: "↑ energy retained", color: col.series[1],
      }),
      Plot.line(curve, { x: "rank", y: "magnitude", stroke: col.series[0], strokeWidth: 1.5 }),
      Plot.line(curve, { x: "rank", y: (d) => y(nines(d.energy)), stroke: col.series[1], strokeWidth: 1.5 }),
      Plot.dot(curve.length === 1 ? curve : [], { x: "rank", y: "magnitude", fill: col.series[0] }),
      Plot.dot(curve.length === 1 && analysis.total ? curve : [], { x: "rank", y: (d) => y(nines(d.energy)), fill: col.series[1] }),
      Plot.ruleX([cut.kept], { stroke: col.series[2], strokeDasharray: "4,3" }),
    ],
  })}</div>`
}
```

The coefficient panels show the sum of absolute magnitudes across RGB channels
on a logarithmic colour scale: brighter means larger. Each original/sparse pair
shares a scale, but the scale resets when the image or basis changes. For the
DCT, the top left holds the lowest frequencies; the wavelet layout groups
coefficients by scale and position.

The plot sorts coefficients from largest to smallest. Read **magnitude** on
the left axis and **cumulative energy retained** on the right. Both rank and
magnitude use logarithmic scales; the energy axis spaces 90%, 99%, and 99.9%
equally to reveal the last few percent of error. The dashed line marks the
actual number retained. A fast drop in magnitude and fast rise in energy mean
that relatively few coefficients describe much of the image.

The slider requests a coefficient budget; the implementation chooses a nearby
magnitude threshold. Ties and narrow magnitude bins can keep more than requested.
The **kept** readout shows the actual count.
Energy is the sum of squared values, so a bright average can dominate it even
when fine detail is missing. PSNR measures squared error, not perceptual quality.

For each channel matrix $X$, the rows of $B_h$ and $B_w$ are orthonormal basis
vectors. The calculation is

$$
C = B_h X B_w^{\mathsf T},\qquad
\hat X = B_h^{\mathsf T}\tilde C B_w,
$$

where $\tilde C$ contains the retained coefficients. This is the companion
article's notation with $B=\Psi^{\mathsf T}$. With $N=3hw$ channel values in
$[0,1]$, orthonormality gives

$$
\mathrm{MSE}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\text{discarded }k} c_k^2,
\qquad \mathrm{PSNR}=10\log_{10}\frac{1}{\mathrm{MSE}}\;\text{dB}.
$$

The readouts use this identity before display clipping and rounding. At 100%
kept the theoretical error is zero (infinite PSNR), though floating-point GPU
calculations still introduce tiny numerical errors. Fourier uses a real
sine/cosine basis; Daubechies 4 means `db4` (four vanishing moments, eight taps).
The wavelets use six levels along each axis with periodic boundaries. None of
these options implements a complete JPEG or JPEG 2000 codec.

<!--
Machinery. OJS cells run in dependency order, not page order.

The flow: `source` and `maxSide` give `image`; `image` gives `res`, the GPU
buffers sized to it; `basisName` gives `analysis` (upload the basis, forward
transform, read the coefficients back once for their histogram); `keepPct`
gives `cut` (a lookup in that histogram) and a frame (inverse transform and
redraw). WebGPU runs submitted work in order, so a frame never sees a basis
that is half uploaded.
-->

{{< include ../_theme/_ojs-setup.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
import { BASES, LEVELS, transpose } from "./compression-bases.js"
```

```{ojs}
// A matrix product on all three channels at once, O = L · R, where one side is
// a basis shared by the channels (batch stride 0). Each 16 × 16 workgroup
// computes a 64 × 64 tile of O, each thread a 4 × 4 block of it, stepping
// through K 16 at a time in workgroup memory. Every side is a multiple of 64
// (see `image`), so there are no edge cases. Entries of R below t count as zero,
// which is the threshold; t = 0 keeps everything.
MATMUL = `
struct P { M: u32, N: u32, K: u32, sL: u32, sR: u32, sO: u32, t: f32, pad: u32 }
@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> p: P;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> L: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> R: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read_write> O: array<f32>;
var<workgroup> tL: array<array<f32, 64>, 16>;
var<workgroup> tR: array<array<f32, 64>, 16>;

@compute @workgroup_size(16, 16)
fn main(@builtin(workgroup_id) g: vec3u, @builtin(local_invocation_id) l: vec3u,
        @builtin(local_invocation_index) li: u32) {
  let m0 = g.y * 64u;
  let n0 = g.x * 64u;
  let lo = g.z * p.sL;
  let ro = g.z * p.sR;
  var acc: array<array<f32, 4>, 4>;
  for (var k0 = 0u; k0 < p.K; k0 += 16u) {
    for (var i = 0u; i < 4u; i++) {
      let e = li + i * 256u;
      tL[e % 16u][e / 16u] = L[lo + (m0 + e / 16u) * p.K + k0 + e % 16u];
      let v = R[ro + (k0 + e / 64u) * p.N + n0 + e % 64u];
      tR[e / 64u][e % 64u] = select(v, 0.0, abs(v) < p.t);
    }
    workgroupBarrier();
    for (var k = 0u; k < 16u; k++) {
      var a: array<f32, 4>;
      var b: array<f32, 4>;
      for (var i = 0u; i < 4u; i++) {
        a[i] = tL[k][l.y + 16u * i];
        b[i] = tR[k][l.x + 16u * i];
      }
      for (var i = 0u; i < 4u; i++) {
        for (var j = 0u; j < 4u; j++) { acc[i][j] += a[i] * b[j]; }
      }
    }
    workgroupBarrier();
  }
  for (var i = 0u; i < 4u; i++) {
    for (var j = 0u; j < 4u; j++) {
      O[g.z * p.sO + (m0 + l.y + 16u * i) * p.N + n0 + l.x + 16u * j] = acc[i][j];
    }
  }
}`
```

```{ojs}
// One panel, drawn straight into its canvas: a triangle that covers it, and one
// fragment per pixel. Mode 0 is an image, clamped to [0, 1]. Mode 1 is a
// coefficient field: the log of the magnitude summed over the channels, counting
// entries below t as zero, through a colour map. Mode 2 is the error of image A
// against image B, magnified by `gain`.
DISPLAY = `
struct D { w: u32, h: u32, mode: u32, t: f32, lo: f32, hi: f32, gain: f32, pad: f32 }
@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> d: D;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> A: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> B: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read> lut: array<vec4f, 256>;

@vertex
fn vs(@builtin(vertex_index) i: u32) -> @builtin(position) vec4f {
  let p = vec2f(f32((i << 1u) & 2u), f32(i & 2u));
  return vec4f(p * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);
}

@fragment
fn fs(@builtin(position) pos: vec4f) -> @location(0) vec4f {
  let n = d.w * d.h;
  let i = u32(pos.y) * d.w + u32(pos.x);
  let a = vec3f(A[i], A[n + i], A[2u * n + i]);
  if (d.mode == 0u) { return vec4f(clamp(a, vec3f(0.0), vec3f(1.0)), 1.0); }
  if (d.mode == 2u) {
    let b = vec3f(B[i], B[n + i], B[2u * n + i]);
    return vec4f(min(abs(a - b) * d.gain, vec3f(1.0)), 1.0);
  }
  let m = abs(a);
  let s = dot(select(m, vec3f(0.0), m < vec3f(d.t)), vec3f(1.0));
  let u = clamp((log(s + 1e-12) - d.lo) / (d.hi - d.lo), 0.0, 1.0);
  return lut[u32(u * 255.0)];
}`
```

```{ojs}
// The device and the two pipelines, once per page. Without WebGPU this is an
// Error, which the status line shows, and nothing downstream runs.
gpu = {
  const adapter = await navigator.gpu?.requestAdapter()
  if (!adapter) return new Error("This playground needs WebGPU, which this browser does not provide.")
  const device = await adapter.requestDevice()
  const format = navigator.gpu.getPreferredCanvasFormat()
  const matmul = device.createComputePipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    compute: { module: device.createShaderModule({ code: MATMUL }), entryPoint: "main" },
  })
  const module = device.createShaderModule({ code: DISPLAY })
  const display = device.createRenderPipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    vertex: { module, entryPoint: "vs" },
    fragment: { module, entryPoint: "fs", targets: [{ format }] },
  })
  // 256 colours for the coefficient panels.
  const colours = Float32Array.from(d3.range(256).flatMap((i) => {
    const { r, g, b } = d3.rgb(d3.interpolateMagma(i / 255))
    return [r / 255, g / 255, b / 255, 1]
  }))
  const lut = device.createBuffer({ size: colours.byteLength, usage: GPUBufferUsage.STORAGE | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST })
  device.queue.writeBuffer(lut, 0, colours)
  return { device, format, matmul, display, lut }
}
```

```{ojs}
// The panels outlive every image, so their zoom and pan persist too. Scroll to
// zoom, drag to pan, double-click to reset. Each space shares one view, so the
// same detail stays side by side: original with reconstruction, coefficients
// with sparse coefficients.
canvases = {
  if (gpu instanceof Error) return new Promise(() => {})
  const names = ["original", "coefficients", "sparse", "reconstruction"]
  const all = Object.fromEntries(names.map((name) => [name, document.createElement("canvas")]))
  for (const [name, c] of Object.entries(all)) {
    c.setAttribute("role", "img")
    c.setAttribute("aria-label", name)
    c.getContext("webgpu").configure({ device: gpu.device, format: gpu.format, alphaMode: "opaque" })
  }
  const zoom = (group) => {
    let view = { s: 1, x: 0, y: 0 }
    const apply = () => {
      for (const c of group) {
        const box = c.parentElement?.getBoundingClientRect()
        const width = box?.width ?? 1
        // Clamp so the image always covers its viewport.
        view.x = Math.min(0, Math.max(width * (1 - view.s), view.x))
        view.y = Math.min(0, Math.max((box?.height ?? 1) * (1 - view.s), view.y))
        c.style.transform = `translate(${view.x}px, ${view.y}px) scale(${view.s})`
        // Nearest-neighbour only when magnifying: it aliases when shrinking.
        const magnified = view.s * width * devicePixelRatio >= c.width
        c.style.imageRendering = magnified ? "pixelated" : "auto"
      }
    }
    for (const c of group) {
      c.addEventListener("wheel", (e) => {
        e.preventDefault()
        const box = c.parentElement.getBoundingClientRect()
        const px = e.clientX - box.left, py = e.clientY - box.top
        const s = Math.min(64, Math.max(1, view.s * Math.exp(-e.deltaY / 400)))
        view = { s, x: px - ((px - view.x) * s) / view.s, y: py - ((py - view.y) * s) / view.s }
        apply()
      }, { passive: false })
      c.addEventListener("pointerdown", (e) => {
        c.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)
        let last = [e.clientX, e.clientY]
        const move = (e) => {
          view.x += e.clientX - last[0]
          view.y += e.clientY - last[1]
          last = [e.clientX, e.clientY]
          apply()
        }
        c.addEventListener("pointermove", move)
        // Fires on release and on cancel, where pointerup would miss a cancel.
        c.addEventListener("lostpointercapture", () => c.removeEventListener("pointermove", move), { once: true })
      })
      c.addEventListener("dblclick", () => { view = { s: 1, x: 0, y: 0 }; apply() })
    }
  }
  zoom([all.original, all.reconstruction])
  zoom([all.coefficients, all.sparse])
  return all
}
```

```{ojs}
// A failed load is kept as a value, so the status line can say what went
// wrong while the panels keep the last image that did load.
loaded = (async () => {
  const blob = typeof source === "string"
    ? await fetch(source, { cache: "no-store" }).then((r) => {
        if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${r.status} ${r.statusText}`)
        return r.blob()
      })
    : await source.blob()
  return createImageBitmap(blob)
})().catch((error) => new Error(`Could not load that image (${error.message}).` + (typeof source === "string"
  ? " Its server may not allow other sites to read it; save it and choose it as a file instead."
  : "")))
```

```{ojs}
// The image, shrunk so its longest side is at most `maxSide`, then trimmed at
// the centre to a multiple of 2^LEVELS on each side so every wavelet level
// halves evenly (and the matrix product needs no edge cases). Planar RGB in
// [0, 1]: all of red, then green, then blue.
image = {
  if (loaded instanceof Error) return new Promise(() => {})
  const bw = loaded.width, bh = loaded.height
  const s = Math.min(1, maxSide / Math.max(bw, bh))
  const step = 2 ** LEVELS
  // At least one step, so a tiny or very narrow image is padded with black
  // instead of trimmed to nothing.
  const w = Math.max(step, Math.floor((bw * s) / step) * step)
  const h = Math.max(step, Math.floor((bh * s) / step) * step)
  const canvas = document.createElement("canvas")
  canvas.width = w
  canvas.height = h
  const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d", { willReadFrequently: true })
  ctx.imageSmoothingQuality = "high"
  // Whole-pixel offsets, so an unscaled image is copied, not resampled.
  ctx.drawImage(loaded, Math.floor((bw - w / s) / 2), Math.floor((bh - h / s) / 2), w / s, h / s, 0, 0, w, h)
  const px = ctx.getImageData(0, 0, w, h).data
  const data = new Float32Array(3 * h * w)
  for (let c = 0; c < 3; c++) for (let i = 0; i < h * w; i++) data[c * h * w + i] = px[i * 4 + c] / 255
  return { data, h, w }
}
```

```{ojs}
// The GPU side of one image: its buffers, the four products (two forward, two
// inverse) and the four panels, each with its own small uniform buffer so they
// can all go in one submission.
res = {
  const { device, matmul, display, lut } = gpu
  const { data, h, w } = image
  const hw = h * w
  const owned = []
  const buffer = (bytes, usage) => {
    const b = device.createBuffer({ size: bytes, usage })
    owned.push(b)
    return b
  }
  const { STORAGE, UNIFORM, COPY_DST, COPY_SRC } = GPUBufferUsage
  const matrix = (n) => buffer(4 * n, STORAGE | COPY_DST | COPY_SRC)
  const B = {
    Bh: matrix(h * h), BhT: matrix(h * h), Bw: matrix(w * w), BwT: matrix(w * w),
    X: matrix(3 * hw), T: matrix(3 * hw), C: matrix(3 * hw), U: matrix(3 * hw), Xh: matrix(3 * hw),
  }
  device.queue.writeBuffer(B.X, 0, data)
  const group = (pipeline, buffers) => device.createBindGroup({
    layout: pipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
    entries: buffers.map((b, binding) => ({ binding, resource: { buffer: b } })),
  })

  // O = L · R on every channel; `batched` names the side that is the image.
  const product = (L, R, O, [M, K, N], batched) => {
    const params = buffer(32, UNIFORM | COPY_DST)
    const bind = group(matmul, [params, L, R, O])
    const set = (t) => {
      const bytes = new ArrayBuffer(32)
      new Uint32Array(bytes, 0, 6).set([M, N, K, batched === "L" ? hw : 0, batched === "R" ? hw : 0, hw])
      new Float32Array(bytes, 24, 1)[0] = t
      device.queue.writeBuffer(params, 0, bytes)
    }
    set(0)
    return { set, run: (pass) => { pass.setBindGroup(0, bind); pass.dispatchWorkgroups(N / 64, M / 64, 3) } }
  }
  const forward = [product(B.Bh, B.X, B.T, [h, h, w], "R"), product(B.T, B.BwT, B.C, [h, w, w], "L")]
  const inverse = [product(B.BhT, B.C, B.U, [h, h, w], "R"), product(B.U, B.Bw, B.Xh, [h, w, w], "L")]

  const panel = (canvas, A, other = A) => {
    const params = buffer(32, UNIFORM | COPY_DST)
    const bind = group(display, [params, A, other, lut])
    canvas.width = w
    canvas.height = h
    return {
      set: ({ mode = 0, t = 0, span = [0, 1], gain = 1 }) => {
        const bytes = new ArrayBuffer(32)
        new Uint32Array(bytes, 0, 3).set([w, h, mode])
        new Float32Array(bytes, 12, 4).set([t, span[0], span[1], gain])
        device.queue.writeBuffer(params, 0, bytes)
      },
      draw: (encoder) => {
        const pass = encoder.beginRenderPass({
          colorAttachments: [{ view: canvas.getContext("webgpu").getCurrentTexture().createView(), loadOp: "clear", storeOp: "store" }],
        })
        pass.setPipeline(display)
        pass.setBindGroup(0, bind)
        pass.draw(3)
        pass.end()
      },
    }
  }
  const panels = {
    original: panel(canvases.original, B.X),
    coefficients: panel(canvases.coefficients, B.C),
    sparse: panel(canvases.sparse, B.C),
    reconstruction: panel(canvases.reconstruction, B.Xh, B.X),
  }
  // Redraw one panel with its current settings. A WebGPU canvas reads back
  // empty once its frame is on screen, so scripts/export-compression-figures.ts
  // calls this and reads the canvas in the same task.
  for (const [name, p] of Object.entries(panels)) {
    canvases[name].redraw = () => {
      const encoder = device.createCommandEncoder()
      p.draw(encoder)
      device.queue.submit([encoder.finish()])
    }
  }

  // Redraws run one at a time, and while one is waiting a newer one replaces
  // it, so a fast drag on a slow GPU renders the latest position instead of
  // every position it passed through.
  let next = null, busy = false, dead = false
  const frame = async (job) => {
    next = job
    if (busy) return
    busy = true
    while (next && !dead) { const run = next; next = null; await run() }
    busy = false
  }
  invalidation.then(() => { dead = true; owned.forEach((b) => b.destroy()) })
  return { ...B, h, w, forward, inverse, panels, frame }
}
```

```{ojs}
// Forward transform for the chosen basis, C = B_h X B_wᵀ, then one readback of
// C for its histogram.
analysis = {
  const { device, matmul } = gpu
  const { h, w } = res
  const q = device.queue
  const Bh = BASES[basisName](h)
  const Bw = w === h ? Bh : BASES[basisName](w)
  q.writeBuffer(res.Bh, 0, Bh)
  q.writeBuffer(res.BhT, 0, transpose(Bh, h))
  q.writeBuffer(res.Bw, 0, Bw)
  q.writeBuffer(res.BwT, 0, transpose(Bw, w))
  const bytes = 12 * h * w
  const read = device.createBuffer({ size: bytes, usage: GPUBufferUsage.MAP_READ | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST })
  const encoder = device.createCommandEncoder()
  const pass = encoder.beginComputePass()
  pass.setPipeline(matmul)
  res.forward.forEach((p) => p.run(pass))
  pass.end()
  encoder.copyBufferToBuffer(res.C, 0, read, 0, bytes)
  q.submit([encoder.finish()])
  await read.mapAsync(GPUMapMode.READ)
  const stats = histogram(new Float32Array(read.getMappedRange()), h, w)
  read.destroy()
  return stats
}
```

```{ojs}
// Everything the threshold slider needs, from one pass over the coefficients
// instead of a sort. Magnitudes go into log-spaced bins holding a count and an
// energy; summed from the top, bin b says how many coefficients are at least
// its lower edge and how much energy they carry. Thresholding at a bin edge is
// nearly exact (the GPU rounds the threshold to f32), and with 2^16 bins the
// edges are 0.04% apart. C is planar,
// all of one channel and then the next.
histogram = function (C, h, w) {
  const BINS = 1 << 16
  const hw = h * w
  let max = 0
  for (const v of C) max = Math.max(max, Math.abs(v))
  // An all-black image has no nonzero coefficient; any finite top will do.
  const top = Math.log(max || 1), bottom = top - Math.log(1e12)
  const scale = (BINS - 1) / (top - bottom)
  const count = new Float64Array(BINS), energy = new Float64Array(BINS)
  const field = new Float32Array(hw)
  for (let i = 0; i < C.length; i++) {
    const a = Math.abs(C[i])
    const b = a > 0 ? Math.min(BINS - 1, Math.max(0, Math.floor((Math.log(a) - bottom) * scale))) : 0
    count[b]++
    energy[b] += a * a
    field[i % hw] += a
  }
  // Sum the discarded tail directly. Subtracting retained energy from total
  // loses tiny errors to cancellation when almost all energy is retained.
  const discarded = new Float64Array(BINS)
  for (let b = 1; b < BINS; b++) discarded[b] = discarded[b - 1] + energy[b - 1]
  for (let b = BINS - 2; b >= 0; b--) {
    count[b] += count[b + 1]
    energy[b] += energy[b + 1]
  }
  // Use the same summation order for numerator and denominator, so retaining
  // everything gives exactly 100% energy rather than a rounding residual.
  const total = energy[0]
  // The colour range of the coefficient panels, from percentiles of the log
  // field; a few enormous low-frequency coefficients would wash out the rest.
  const sample = d3.range(0, hw, 7).map((i) => Math.log(field[i] + 1e-12)).sort(d3.ascending)
  const edge = (b) => Math.exp(bottom + b / scale)
  // The decay curve and the energy kept up to each rank: one point per bin
  // where the rank has grown by 1%.
  const curve = []
  for (let b = BINS - 1, last = 0; b >= 0; b--) {
    if (count[b] >= Math.max(1, last * 1.01)) {
      curve.push({ rank: count[b], magnitude: edge(b), energy: total ? energy[b] / total : 1 })
      last = count[b]
    }
  }
  const lo = d3.quantileSorted(sample, 0.01), hi = d3.quantileSorted(sample, 0.999)
  return {
    n: C.length, count, energy, discarded, total, edge, curve,
    span: [lo, hi > lo ? hi : lo + 1],
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
// The threshold for the slider: the highest bin edge that keeps at least the
// asked-for number of coefficients. The basis is orthonormal, so the squared
// error of the reconstruction is exactly the energy thrown away (Parseval),
// before the display clips it to [0, 1].
cut = {
  const { n, count, energy, discarded, total, edge } = analysis
  const want = Math.max(1, Math.round((keepPct / 100) * n))
  let b = count.length - 1
  while (b > 0 && count[b] < want) b--
  const mse = discarded[b] / n
  return {
    t: b === 0 ? 0 : edge(b),
    kept: count[b],
    energy: total ? energy[b] / total : 1,
    psnr: mse > 0 ? 10 * Math.log10(1 / mse) : Infinity,
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// The inverse, B_hᵀ · (C with the small entries zeroed) · B_w, then every panel.
// The time is from submission until the GPU reports the work done.
res.frame(async () => {
  const { device, matmul } = gpu
  const { span } = analysis
  const P = res.panels
  const start = performance.now()
  res.inverse[0].set(cut.t)
  P.original.set({})
  P.coefficients.set({ mode: 1, span })
  P.sparse.set({ mode: 1, t: cut.t, span })
  P.reconstruction.set(view === "reconstruction" ? {} : { mode: 2, gain: 10 })
  const encoder = device.createCommandEncoder()
  const pass = encoder.beginComputePass()
  pass.setPipeline(matmul)
  res.inverse.forEach((p) => p.run(pass))
  pass.end()
  Object.values(P).forEach((p) => p.draw(encoder))
  device.queue.submit([encoder.finish()])
  await device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()
  status.textContent = `${res.w} × ${res.h} · ${Math.round(performance.now() - start)} ms per update`
})
```
